1(a)(i).assumed: Acceleration is the gradient of a v–t graph.

1(a)(iii).assumed: Stopping distance = total area under v–t graph: thinking rectangle plus braking triangle.

1(a)(iv).assumed: Work done by brakes = force × braking distance = initial KE.

1(b).assumed: Same reaction time; same deceleration (gradient), so braking time halves.

1(c)(i).assumed: Tiredness lengthens reaction time, extending the constant-speed section only.

1(c)(ii).assumed: More friction gives a larger braking force and steeper negative gradient; thinking section unchanged.

2.assumed: Time balls between marks once terminal; vary diameter; plot v against d²; straight line through origin; K from gradient.

3(a).assumed: Component of velocity along a direction uses cos of the angle from that direction.

3(b).assumed: v² = u² + 2as for the vertical motion with a = g.

3(c).assumed: Combine horizontal and vertical components for speed, then ½mv² (or initial KE + mgh).

3(d).assumed: Momentum is a vector; gravity's force changes velocity, so momentum changes.

4(a)(ii).assumed: Absolute uncertainties add when subtracting two readings.

4(a)(iii).assumed: Two identical springs in series halve the stiffness; weight = kx; mass = W/g.

4(a)(iv).assumed: Elastic energy = ½kx² (summed for both springs).

4(b)(i).assumed: From E = FL/(Ax), F–x gradient = EA/L; rearrange for A with N mm⁻¹ to N m⁻¹.

4(b)(ii).assumed: Work done = area under force–extension graph, estimated by counting squares.

5(a)(i).assumed: Water waves are transverse: oscillations perpendicular to direction of travel.

5(a)(ii).assumed: Plane polarised means oscillations in one plane only.

5(c)(i).assumed: Path difference in wavelengths: half-integer gives destructive interference.

5(c)(ii).assumed: Phase difference = 2π × path difference/λ, reduced by whole cycles.

6(a).assumed: A filament lamp's I–V graph curves as resistance rises with current.

6(b).assumed: A reading's decimal places reveal the meter's resolution and range.

6(c)(i).assumed: Parallel currents add; read lamp current from its I–V graph; R = V/I.

6(c)(ii).assumed: Open-circuit p.d. equals e.m.f.; r = (E − V)/I.

6(d).assumed: Lower total resistance raises current, increasing lost volts Ir, so terminal p.d. falls.

7.assumed: Find fundamental by adjusting frequency for loudest sound; relate 1/f to tube length; v from gradient; worst line for percentage uncertainty.

8(a)(i).assumed: Each electron absorbs one photon; emission occurs if photon energy exceeds work function.

8(a)(ii).assumed: Threshold frequency is the minimum frequency of radiation that releases electrons.

8(b)(i).assumed: Multiply eV by 1.60 × 10⁻¹⁹ to get joules.

8(b)(ii).assumed: hf = hf₀ + KEmax for photon frequency; λ = c/f with THz conversions.

8(c)(i).assumed: Intensity does not change photon energy, so KEmax is unchanged.

8(c)(ii).assumed: Doubling intensity doubles photon rate and so doubles electron emission rate.
